questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cofactor Method To Solve for an Unknown Quantity
questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & k & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]$
equals $\frac{1}{18}$ and $det(A)=-18.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=-18
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ k & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2+k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31} \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\cdot (2+k).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{13}^{′}=\frac{1}{18}$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{18}(2+k) & =\frac{1}{18} \\ 2+k & =-1 \\ k & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
equals $-1$ and $det(A)=4-2k.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that we are given the determinant of $A:$

$$
det(A)=4-2k
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2-0) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{4-2k}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{k-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k-2} & =-1 \\ 1 & =2-k \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Element of the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
Determine the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$

${a}_{32}^{′}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A)=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}| & =3|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|+(-3)|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(2+2)-0-3(2-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{32}^{t}={c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(6-0) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{32}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-6) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Determine the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

if its determinant is $3.$

${a}_{21}^{′}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{21}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{12}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{12} & =(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\,(1\cdot 1-0\cdot 2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{21}^{′} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}\,{c}_{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ k & -2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

equals $-2.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ k & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ k & -1\end{aligned}|+(-2)|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)((-1)(-1)-(-2)(-2))+2((-2)(-1)-(-2)k)+(-2)((-2)(-2)-(-1)k) \\  & =(-2)(1-4)+2(2+2k)+(-2)(4+k) \\  & =6+4+4k-8-2k \\  & =2k+2\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{32}^{t}={c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-((-2)(-2)-(-2)k) \\  & =-(4+2k) \\  & =-2k-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{32}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{-2k-4}{2k+2} \\  & =-\frac{k+2}{k+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=-2$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k+2}{k+1} & =-2 \\ \frac{k+2}{k+1} & =2 \\ k+2 & =2k+2 \\ k & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
